summary: A 1966 steel tower on Monte Vista Peak in the Chiricahua Mountains, still an active Forest Service lookout, reached on foot by trail.

facts.design: 40-ft steel tower with USDA CL-100 metal cab, 14 ft by 14 ft (1966 replacement)

access.note: Reached on foot by trail. The cab is an active Forest Service station. The sources give no visitor entry rule for the cab.

visit.trail_note: Trailheads in the Turkey Creek area (Morse Canyon Trail #43 or Pole Bridge Trail #264) and in the Rucker Canyon area, including one at the end of Forest Road 628 off FR-74E.

events.note: 30-ft Aermotor tower replaced the crow's nest
Support cabin at the base of the lookout, built by the CCC. This is the NRHP-listed cabin, not the tower.
Erroneous report that the support cabin had been destroyed in a forest fire (per Wikipedia)
Current 40-ft steel tower with CL-100 14x14 cab
Monte Vista Lookout Cabin added to the National Register, January 28, 1988
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, January 31, 2003
Horseshoe II fire ravaged much of the Chiricahua Mountains and destroyed Barfoot Lookout; it came close to Monte Vista but bypassed the site
2013 summary: lookout is active and generally manned during the high fire danger season

evidence.supports: current tower 40 ft steel with CL-100 14x14 cab, built 1966
evidence.quote: The 40’ steel tower with a CL-100 metal 14’x14’ cab at Monte Vista Lookout was built in 1966.

evidence.supports: 1922 Aermotor replaced the 1916 crow's nest tower
evidence.quote: It replaced a 30’ Aermotor tower built in 1922 that in turn had replaced a crow’s nest tower dating to 1916.
The Coronado National Forest station is in active service

evidence.supports: active lookout, generally manned in high fire danger season
evidence.quote: It is an active lookout and is generally manned during the high fire danger season.

evidence.supports: Coronado National Forest, southern Chiricahua Mountains
evidence.quote: located in the Coronado National Forest in the southern portion of the Chiricahua Mountains

evidence.supports: three towers over the site's life
evidence.quote: has gone through three different iterations

evidence.supports: Turkey Creek trailheads (Morse Canyon #43, Pole Bridge #264) on foot
evidence.quote: The route that the Green Valley Hiking Club uses to hike to the lookout is from one of two trailheads in the Turkey Creek area (Morse Canyon Trail #43 or Pole Bridge Trail #264)

evidence.supports: current tower is forty feet tall
evidence.quote: mounted on a forty-foot tall steel tower
It was originally constructed in 1916 as a “Crow’s Nest” tower.

evidence.supports: 2011 Horseshoe II fire destroyed Barfoot Lookout
evidence.quote: The Horseshoe II fire of 2011 ravaged a large portion of the Chiricahua Mountains and destroyed the Barfoot Lookout

evidence.supports: fire came close to the lookout site but bypassed it
evidence.quote: The fire came close to the lookout site but bypassed it.

evidence.supports: trailheads in Turkey Creek area and Rucker Canyon area; one at the end of Forest Road 628
evidence.quote: a trailhead at the end of Forest Road 628 (a side road off of FR-74E)

evidence.supports: support cabin built 1933 by CCC; NRHP listing is for the cabin
cabin sits at base of lookout
evidence.quote: The cabin sits at the base of the Lookout, in the southern portion of the Chiricahua Mountains in the Coronado National Forest.

evidence.supports: 1956 erroneous report that the cabin was destroyed in a forest fire
evidence.quote: In 1956, it was erroneously reported that the cabin had been destroyed during a forest fire.

corrections.why: Both the NHLR page and the Green Valley Hiking Club summary give a 40-foot tower. 40 ft is 12.2 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia dates a CCC-built cabin to 1933. That is the support cabin with its own NRHP listing. The tower's 1966 date from the NHLR and the GVRHC summary is used for the tower.

sources.title: Monte Vista Fire Lookout (summary prepared June 2013)

notes_for_editor: The 1956 claim about a forest fire is cited to Wikipedia only; the reference Wikipedia cites was not opened. The newest staffing evidence is the 2013 GVRHC summary; check the current season status before trusting it. Access 'public' means trail access on foot, not a cab tour; no source states a cab-entry rule. The NHLR and GVRHC agree on the 1916, 1922 and 1966 towers.
